findings.source: reflection_audit.py supplied() lines 54-58 and relative_import_unknown() lines 60-66: supplied() looks only at args[index], the keyword and a ** spread, so a positional *spread that ends before slot 4 hides the level; relative_import_unknown() and keys() handle only builtins.__import__, although importlib.__import__ is inside the existing importlib.* enumeration (api()) with the same (name, globals, locals, fromlist, level) signature

L1-near-importlib-dunder-import-level1: importlib.__import__('workspace_config', globals(), None, (), 1).configured_workspace(object(), tenant, settings) -> ACCEPT

findings.minimalCorrection: supplied(): if any ast.Starred appears in call.args at a position <= index, return [None]. Treat importlib.__import__ exactly like builtins.__import__ in keys() and relative_import_unknown(). Regressions: these two refuse; the level-0 literal and existing controls and the 72028 positive still ACCEPT. No general import resolver is needed.

findings.source: callee_identity.py error() lines 72-77 and rebound() lines 29-34: the new lexical index is consulted only for the callee's DEFINING file (receiver) and, for a Name call, only when the name is a def in the caller (f.defs['']). When the call-site name is an import alias in the caller (from .workspace_api import WorkspaceAPI), a global-declared import or star import in the caller's binding scope of that name is recorded by lexical_bindings but never applied

findings.minimalCorrection: For a Name call, also check the CALLER file: find the scope that binds the call-site name, and refuse CALLEE_REBOUND when that scope has a binding event of the name (from the lexical index, global-redirected) or a star import beyond the exact-frozen multiset for that file. This needs counts, not the current writes set, so the frozen import binding itself is allowed. Regressions: this case and the two binder fixtures refuse; the plain cross-module import control, existing controls and the 72028 positive still ACCEPT.
